content:
**Removed masking local CAS from remote-authoritative audit-cursor**

**What**: In PR1 of issue-259-d2, removed the redundant LOCAL CAS `git update-ref CURSOR_REF to from` from advanceCursor and the local `rev-parse` reader from readCursor, making the remote `push --force-with-lease` the sole authority. readCursor now parses the sha from `ls-remote --exit-code` stdout directly. Removed dead `syncCursor` (fetch) and `GOVERNANCE_REFSPEC`.
**Why**: The local CAS masked the remote lease in every test (a plain --force mutant stayed green) and broke the human `accept` path on a plain actions/checkout clone (local governance ref absent → update-ref threw before the remote lease). Owner ruling: separate the guard (remote authority) from any cache; authority decides first.
**Where**: brain/scripts/governance/postmerge/cursor.mjs (readCursor 26-40, advanceCursor 66-79, syncCursor removed); brain/scripts/governance/postmerge/cursor.test.mjs (rewrote tautological B5 + acceptManually RACE as two-clone cross-runner tests; added plain-checkout accept + lease-no-divergence tests; fixed positive-accept and CLI-accept assertions to check the REMOTE cursor).
**Learned**: `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<expect>` uses the explicit expected value, NOT the remote-tracking ref, so it works on a clone that never fetched the ref. A plain `git clone` never creates refs/governance/*. Mutation bar: swapping --force-with-lease→--force makes the two-clone race go RED (stale advance wins); reinstating the local CAS makes the plain-checkout accept go RED (symptom-2). No external reader of the local ref exists (cursor.mjs not yet wired into any workflow). Do NOT run root `npm test` — it can rewrite local git identity.
